submissions.title: Data center moratorium takes first steps after Fort Worth City Council's unanimous vote
submissions.excerpt: City Council voted unanimously ... to initiate the process to enact a 90-day moratorium on the construction of data centers within the city.
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Fort Worth, TX city council voted unanimously on Aug 11, 2026 to begin the process toward a 90-day moratorium on new data center permitting/rezoning applications, and separately voted 10-1 to create a Data Center & Infrastructure Commission (DCIC) chaired by TCU's Dr. Mike Slattery. The moratorium is not yet in effect: by the city's own process it would run roughly Feb 16-May 17, 2027, contingent on required public hearings and a final vote needing a three-fourths council majority. Corroborated by Fort Worth Report, KERA News, WBAP, The Texan, and NBC 5 DFW. submissions.title: Indy council advances pause on data centers, sends to commission for final approval
submissions.excerpt: voted 23-1 ... to prevent tech companies from building any new data centers through the end of 2027.
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Indianapolis-Marion County City-County Council voted 23-1 on Aug 10, 2026 to halt new data center permitting through Dec 31, 2027, pending a Metropolitan Development Commission final vote expected as early as Aug 19, 2026 (a human should check whether that vote has since happened). Three already-approved projects are explicitly exempted: DC Blox (Warren Township), Metrobloks (Martindale-Brightwood), and Sabey (Decatur Township) -- worth checking whether any of these are, or should be, in the tracker. submissions.title: Louisiana PSC kills ruling that would force Meta to turn over key data center information
submissions.excerpt: commissioners voted 3-1 ... to overrule a judge's decision, allowing Meta to withhold information.
submissions.note: Concerns the tracked project 'Meta Hyperion' (Richland Parish, Louisiana; UNDER_CONSTRUCTION as of this run's snapshot). The Louisiana Public Service Commission voted 3-1 along party lines on Aug 12, 2026 to overrule an administrative law judge's July 10 subpoena order, letting Meta withhold internal figures on the data center's power draw and job projections from public/regulatory disclosure. This is a transparency and ratepayer-scrutiny development, not a metric change -- flagged because it's directly relevant to the project's risk profile and to the accuracy of any power/jobs figures already on file for it, which the company itself is contesting the basis for.
